{
  "research_question": "How does mouse navigation performance vary across five stimulation paradigms (Combined, ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only, and Sham) as measured by Time-to-Target, Success, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, and Angular Dispersion (AD)?",
  "stim_paradigms_compared": ["Combined", "ICMS Only", "Dim Visual Only", "Bright Visual Only", "Sham"],
  "response_variables": ["Time-to-Target", "Success", "Path Efficiency", "Average Speed", "AD"],
  "descriptive_findings": [
    "Combined stimulation yielded the highest success rate (0.780) and fastest Time-to-Target (2.562 s), with high Path Efficiency (0.502) and Average Speed (12.833 units/s), and the highest AD (0.399)",
    "Bright Visual Only produced similarly strong performance: success rate 0.785 (highest among all paradigms), Time-to-Target 2.614 s, Path Efficiency 0.504 (highest), Average Speed 12.679 units/s, and AD 0.387",
    "Dim Visual Only showed intermediate performance: success 0.673, Time-to-Target 3.140 s, Path Efficiency 0.434, Average Speed 11.968 units/s, and AD 0.336 (lowest among visual conditions)",
    "ICMS Only performed comparably to Dim Visual Only: success 0.685, Time-to-Target 3.053 s, Path Efficiency 0.432, Average Speed 12.039 units/s, and AD 0.354",
    "Sham stimulation produced markedly inferior performance across all metrics: success 0.273 (lowest by far), Time-to-Target 4.682 s (slowest), Path Efficiency 0.308, Average Speed 10.737 units/s (slowest), and AD 0.236 (lowest)",
    "Success rates showed substantial stratification: Bright Visual Only ≈ Combined > Dim Visual Only ≈ ICMS Only >> Sham",
    "AD values ranged from 0.236 (Sham) to 0.399 (Combined), with higher AD consistently associated with better navigation performance",
    "Average Speed was highest under Combined and Bright Visual Only conditions, lowest under Sham"
  ],
  "strongest_group_differences": [
    "Success rate: Sham (0.273) versus Combined (0.780) shows a 2.85-fold difference and versus Bright Visual Only (0.785) shows a 2.87-fold difference—the largest effect in the dataset",
    "Time-to-Target: Sham (4.682 s) was 1.83× slower than Combined (2.562 s) and 1.79× slower than Bright Visual Only (2.614 s)",
    "Path Efficiency: Sham (0.308) was substantially lower than all active stimulation conditions, with Combined and Bright Visual Only exceeding 0.50",
    "The performance gap between Sham and all active stimulation conditions is dramatic across every metric, whereas differences among active conditions are more modest",
    "Bright Visual Only and Combined conditions are remarkably similar, suggesting visual stimulation alone may suffice for near-optimal performance"
  ],
  "practical_interpretation": "Active stimulation—whether combined multimodal, bright visual alone, dim visual alone, or ICMS alone—substantially improves mouse navigation performance compared to Sham. The similarity between Combined and Bright Visual Only conditions suggests that bright visual stimulation may be the dominant contributor to performance in the combined paradigm, or that visual and ICMS stimuli are not strongly synergistic. Dim visual and ICMS-only conditions produce intermediate, roughly equivalent performance. The consistent pattern where higher AD accompanies better performance suggests angular dispersion may index exploratory behavior or motor vigor that facilitates target acquisition. Sham performance indicates chance-level or near-chance navigation success, establishing that the task genuinely requires sensory guidance.",
  "limitations": [
    "Data are aggregated means without variance estimates, precluding assessment of statistical significance or effect sizes with confidence intervals",
    "Sample sizes vary dramatically across paradigms (Sham: 3505 trials vs. Combined: 48846 trials), potentially affecting precision of estimates",
    "No information on trial structure, learning effects, or within-subject designs; cannot distinguish between-subject and within-subject variance",
    "AD operationalized as 'angular dispersion' lacks explicit definition of measurement units or calculation method",
    "No distributional information (skewness, outliers) for any performance variable",
    "Missing data on individual mice's exposure to each paradigm, preventing assessment of balance or counterbalancing",
    "No temporal information (e.g., trial order, session effects) to assess fatigue or learning",
    "Temperature and prompt template parameters (0.75, prompts/stim_paradigm_basic.md) suggest this may be LLM-simulated or processed data rather than raw behavioral recordings—uncertainty about data provenance"
  ],
  "recommended_next_analysis": "Conduct inferential statistical analysis accounting for the nested structure (trials within mice within paradigms), using mixed-effects models or ANOVA with mouse as a random effect. Compute Cohen's d or standardized mean differences with confidence intervals to quantify effect sizes. Perform pairwise comparisons with multiple testing correction to identify which paradigm differences are statistically significant. Examine trial-level distributions to assess normality assumptions and identify potential outliers. If individual trial data are available, analyze learning curves and test for interaction between paradigm and trial number. Visualize results with boxplots or violin plots showing within-paradigm variability. Finally, explicitly model the relationship between AD and other performance metrics to test whether angular dispersion mediates or moderates stimulation effects."
}
